content:
alex: Heads-up — we're seeing a sharp tokens/sec drop (~3-4x) on prod after merging runtime PR #4123. Continuous batcher queues are backing up, lots of singletons instead of coalesced batches. :warning:
ci-bot: perf/regressions job 9821 triggered: tokens_per_sec decreased from ~480k -> ~130k on the long-seq workload (compare baseline run 1861998000). See: https://ci.internal/perf/9821 :rotating_light:
mira: ugh. any obvious error logs or kernel fallbacks?
sam: i'm seeing a ton of 'kernel fallback' traces in the scheduler logs right after the merge. looks like kernel selection is preferring the small-batch kernel which is slower for our token lengths.
alex: exact log snippet from canary (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-16T19:12:03Z] sched: batch_coalescer: queued=72 head_wait=182ms avg_batch_size=1.1
[2026-03-16T19:12:03Z] kernel_picker: preferred_kernel=fast_kv_v2 selected=safe_small_batch_kv
[2026-03-16T19:12:03Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.02 prefetch_misses=58
[2026-03-16T19:12:04Z] perf: tokens/sec=127482
```
nora: that head_wait number is wild — we usually see <40ms. something in the coalescer or scheduler heuristics seems to flip to tiny windows.
sam: ran a quick perf profile on canary: `perf record -g -- ./runtime --bench longseq` shows heavy time in `small_batch_kernel::compute` and lots of CPU waiting on the coalescer lock.
ci-bot: perf diff (baseline vs current):
```
- kernel fast_kv_v2: 42% CPU -> 8% CPU
- kernel small_batch_kv: 5% CPU -> 64% CPU
- avg_batch_size: 8.1 -> 1.2
- avg_latency_p50: 18ms -> 92ms
```
mira: does the PR change the kernel selection threshold or the windowing heuristic? iirc #4123 touched kernel routing heuristics and introduced a fallback for certain seq_len distributions.
sam: yes — the change added a conservative path that prefers small-batch kernels when sequence variance is detected. the variance detector seems too sensitive with our telemetry noise.
devon: can we patch the detector threshold quickly? maybe add a short cooldown so one noisy sample doesn't flip routing globally.
alex: patch idea: increase variance threshold by 2x and add 200ms cooldown per device before switching kernels. will that avoid thrash?
nora: also look at KV cache hitrate — it's 2% in the snippet. if kv misses spike, batches shrink and selection will flip. need to confirm if the cache regression is root cause or symptom.
sam: steps i've started:
1) `git bisect` between 1861989000..1862004000 to confirm culprit commit (started, current suspect commit abc123f)
2) run microbench with seeded seq lengths to reproduce fast_kv_v2 rejection
3) collect coalescer lock contention traces (perf + flamegraphs)

alex: CI perf job shows the same pattern on the nightly longseq test — so it's reproducible outside prod.
ci-bot: triggered regression alert to #incidents and created perf ticket PERF-2897.
mira: can we hold the rollout to the rest of prod? is the merge already live everywhere?
alex: it's in canary and half of dedicated pools. i've set the rollout to paused. recommending revert if we can't get mitigation in <2 hours.
devon: quick mitigation that might be less risky than a revert: force kernel routing override via feature flag to prefer fast_kv_v2 on canary pools. we have a flag system for kernel hints.
sam: tested the override locally — tokens/sec recovers to ~460k and avg_batch_size goes back to 7.6.
nora: that suggests the kernel detector flip is principal symptom. but we still need to root cause the KV misses. could be unrelated memory layout change in #4123.
alex: agreed. plan: 1) flip feature flag on affected pools now, 2) continue bisect to identify exact commit and revert if we find a simple fix isn't trivial, 3) follow-up PR to stabilize detector thresholds + cooldowns, 4) add unit/integration test to simulate noisy seq_len telemetry.
mira: i'm happy with the flag flip for immediate relief. alex, can you push the flag? i'll notify support to watch for customer impact.
alex: flag override pushed to canary/dedicated-1 at 19:25Z. monitoring dashboards show tokens/sec recovering. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: rollout paused by alex @ 19:26Z.
devon: after flag flip, coalescer head_wait dropped to ~34ms and avg_batch_size jumped to ~7.8.
sam: leaving `git bisect` running — current suspect range narrowed to commits between abc123f and def456a (both touched kernel routing + kv prefetch).
nora: I'll run a memory/alloc profiler to see if something affected KV cache localities.
alex: thanks all. we'll keep this thread updated. if anyone sees a new regression post-flag, ping here. :eyes:
